idea: Paid private community for generalist analysts
pain: Generalists are isolated and have nobody to test ideas with
v1: A curated group of 30 analysts with monthly sessions
verdict: Warm seed group and a real need, but communities are labour-intensive and churn hard.

why.distribution: She can personally invite 30-50 credible analysts, which is exactly how these start.
why.demand: Inferred; analysts value peer networks but rarely pay for them.
why.fmf: Her credibility is what would make members join and stay - curation is the product.
why.defensibility: Network effects are real once a community reaches critical mass.
why.leverage: One community serves all members, but moderation is constant work.
why.time_to_revenue: 3-6 months to assemble a credible founding group.
why.tailwind: Flat; professional communities are proliferating and attention is scarce.
why.ceiling: £100/mo x 165 members = £198k, and 165 paying analysts is far beyond her network.

ceiling_arithmetic: £100/mo x 165 members = £198k. Her network is ~50 people; 165 paying members requires reaching well beyond it. Realistic: 30-50 = £36-60k, with heavy moderation time.
carries: Genuine network effects if it reaches critical mass, and she is the right convenor.
kills: Member count needed exceeds her network, and communities demand constant unpaid attention.
test: Invite 30 analysts to a free founding cohort and see how many attend twice.
test_pass: Twenty attend repeatedly and ask about a paid tier.
